1	# Task 11: Magic portal with swirling particles and glow
2	
3	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, rendering to the canvas with id #app. The scene is a magic portal standing in an ancient stone ruin at dusk. Build a tall ring portal (a standing circular frame of weathered stone or runic metal) on a stone platform, with moody dusk lighting and a few ruined pillars around it. The disc inside the ring is a swirling, glowing energy surface, such as a rotating vortex in cyan and violet with a bright core, animated continuously. Glowing particles spiral around and into the portal, and a few motes rise from the platform and drift upward, fading out. The portal casts colored light onto the nearby stones and platform, and the light should pulse slowly. Add a subtle slow orbiting camera or gentle camera sway so depth is apparent. Aim for a polished, atmospheric look: strong bloom-like glow around the portal, high contrast against a darker surround, a coherent color palette, and soft haze. Keep it smooth at interactive frame rates. Also expose window.__TASK_STATE__ = { portalActive: true, particleCount: <number of live particles>, time: <elapsed seconds> } and update it every frame.

Group nesting works fine with children passed as builders. For the world, I'm leaning toward rotating the whole group for a subtle camera-sway effect rather than orbit controls, though I need to double check the rotation happens around the right origin point.

For bloom I'll set intensity around 1.1, threshold 0.55, radius 0.7, paired with a haze-colored fog at low density so the portal glow reads at distance without washing out, plus a mild vignette. For particles, I'll reuse three shared glow materials (cyan, violet, white) across spheres, fading them by shrinking scale from an initial unit size down to their final small diameters.

I'm weighing draw-call cost for ~90-100 particle spheres with default segment counts versus using simpler primitives like boxes, since at tiny on-screen sizes (a few pixels with bloom) the shape barely matters visually, so I'll likely stick with default spheres rather than risk unknown segment parameter names.

For the particle motion, I'm designing a spiral-into-the-portal behavior: each particle orbits the disc's central axis at a shrinking radius while its depth collapses toward the disc plane, giving the sucked-in spiral effect, starting from randomized radii and depths around the portal.

I'll fade particle scale in and out with a smooth easing curve and respawn particles once their lifetime completes, keeping the swarm steady and continuous rather than dying out. For separate rising motes drifting off the platform, I'll scatter them randomly across the surface, give them gentle upward drift with sideways sway, short randomized lifespans, and staggered start times so they don't all pop in at once.

For the ring glow I'm giving the inner rim a cyan/violet emissive tint with pulsing driven by the shader's time uniform rather than fixed intensity, and I'm planning small emissive rune glyphs placed around the ring face at twelve positions, sized and rotated as little tangent bars.
